fanoutqa_017948.x:
Wright brothers :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
The brothers gained the mechanical skills essential to their success by working for years in their [Dayton, Ohio](/wiki/Dayton,_Ohio "Dayton, Ohio")-based shop with printing presses, bicycles, motors, and other machinery. Their work with bicycles, in particular, influenced their belief that an unstable vehicle such as a flying machine could be controlled and balanced with practice.[[14]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrouch2003169-14) This was a trend, as many other aviation pioneers were also dedicated cyclists and involved in the bicycle business in various ways.[[15]](#cite_note-15) From 1900 until their first powered flights in late 1903, the brothers conducted extensive [glider tests](/wiki/Glider_(aircraft)#19th_century "Glider (aircraft)") that also developed their skills as pilots. Their shop mechanic [Charles Taylor](/wiki/Charlie_Taylor_(mechanic) "Charlie Taylor (mechanic)") became an important part of the team, building their first airplane engine in close collaboration with the brothers.[[16]](#cite_note-16)

The Wright brothers' status as inventors of the airplane has been subject to numerous counter-claims. Much controversy persists over the many [competing claims of early aviators](/wiki/Claims_to_the_first_powered_flight "Claims to the first powered flight"). Edward Roach, historian for the [Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park](/wiki/Dayton_Aviation_Heritage_National_Historical_Park "Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park"), argues that the Wrights were excellent self-taught engineers who could run a small company well, but did not have the business skills or temperament necessary to dominate the rapidly growing aviation industry at the time.[[17]](#cite_note-17)

The [Kazakh national ice hockey team](/wiki/Kazakhstan_men%27s_national_ice_hockey_team "Kazakhstan men's national ice hockey team") have competed in [ice hockey](/wiki/Ice_hockey "Ice hockey") in the 1998 and [2006 Winter Olympics](/wiki/2006_Winter_Olympics "2006 Winter Olympics"), as well as in the [2006 Men's World Ice Hockey Championships](/wiki/2006_Men%27s_World_Ice_Hockey_Championships "2006 Men's World Ice Hockey Championships"). The [Kazakhstan Hockey Championship](/wiki/Kazakhstan_Hockey_Championship "Kazakhstan Hockey Championship") is held since 1992. Staten Island Technical High School began in 1982 as an annex of Ralph R. McKee Vocational-Technical High School, located in the [New Dorp](/wiki/New_Dorp,_Staten_Island "New Dorp, Staten Island") neighborhood of Staten Island, after [New Dorp High School](/wiki/New_Dorp_High_School "New Dorp High School"), which had occupied the building since it was built in the 1930s, moved to its current location on New Dorp Lane. The technical courses were taught in the annex, while the vocational courses stayed in St. George. Through the advocacy of parents, staff, and students, Staten Island Tech was made an independent high school by the New York City Board of Education in May 1988. Nicholas M. Bilotti, who had been serving as director of the annex, was appointed principal of the new high school.

Born in [Stonewall, Texas](/wiki/Stonewall,_Texas "Stonewall, Texas"), Johnson worked as a teacher and a congressional aide before winning election to the U.S. House of Representatives in 1937. In 1948, he was controversially declared the winner in the Democratic primary for the [U.S. Senate election](/wiki/1948_United_States_Senate_election_in_Texas "1948 United States Senate election in Texas") in Texas before winning the general election.[[1]](#cite_note-2) He became [Senate majority whip](/wiki/Senate_majority_whip "Senate majority whip") in 1951, Senate Democratic leader in 1953 and majority leader in 1954. Senator Kennedy bested Johnson and his other rivals for the [1960](/wiki/1960_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries "1960 Democratic Party presidential primaries") Democratic presidential nomination before surprising many by offering to make Johnson his vice presidential running mate. **Theodore Roosevelt Jr.** (October 27, 1858 – January 6, 1919) was the 26th [president of the United States](/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States"), serving from 1901 to 1909. Previously serving six months as [vice president](/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States "Vice President of the United States") under [William McKinley](/wiki/William_McKinley "William McKinley"), Roosevelt became president after [McKinley's assassination](/wiki/McKinley%27s_assassination "McKinley's assassination") in 1901. He was 42 years old upon [his first inauguration](/wiki/First_inauguration_of_Theodore_Roosevelt "First inauguration of Theodore Roosevelt"), making him the youngest person to hold the office.

A sickly child with debilitating [asthma](/wiki/Asthma "Asthma"), Roosevelt overcame health problems through a regime of vigorous exercise, which he called "[the strenuous life](/wiki/The_Strenuous_Life "The Strenuous Life")". He was [homeschooled](/wiki/Homeschooled "Homeschooled") and began a lifelong naturalist avocation before attending [Harvard University](/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University"). His book *[The Naval War of 1812](/wiki/The_Naval_War_of_1812 "The Naval War of 1812")* established his reputation as a historian and popular writer. Roosevelt became leader of the reform faction of [Republicans](/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") in the [New York State Legislature](/wiki/New_York_State_Legislature "New York State Legislature"). After the simultaneous deaths of his first wife [Alice Hathaway Lee Roosevelt](/wiki/Alice_Hathaway_Lee_Roosevelt "Alice Hathaway Lee Roosevelt") and mother [Martha Bulloch Roosevelt](/wiki/Martha_Bulloch_Roosevelt "Martha Bulloch Roosevelt"), he recuperated by buying and operating a cattle ranch in [the Dakotas](/wiki/The_Dakotas "The Dakotas"). Roosevelt served as the [assistant secretary of the Navy](/wiki/Assistant_
